latin: Per nomen <N\N>, id est Vir, quod tribus litteris scribitur he, uau, et aleph, quod nomen deo propriissime attribuitur, et maxime conuenienter non solum ad Cabalistas, qui hoc expresse sepius dicunt, sed etiam ad theologiam Dionysii Areopagitae, per uiam Cabalae trinitatis mysterium, cum possibilitate incarnationis, nobis declaratur.
latin_note: The bracketed siglum '<N\N>' in the corpus OCR represents the Hebrew word the Latin itself glosses as 'Vir' (man), spelled with He, Vau, and Aleph (farmer1998:27122). The 1486 print reads the initial letter as V, for Vir; the 1487 reprint has U instead (farmer1998:27145).
translation: By the name <N\N> — that is, 'Man' — spelled with the three letters He, Vau, and Aleph, a name most properly given to God, and most fittingly so not only among the Cabalists, who often say this outright, but also in the theology of Dionysius the Areopagite: by way of the Cabala the mystery of the Trinity, together with the possibility of the Incarnation, is declared to us.
translation_note: This translation is prepared independently from the Latin (farmer1998:27122); a line in this packet listed among Farmer's notes 'to paraphrase, not reproduce' (farmer1998:27176) closely reproduces the wording of Farmer's own published English translation of this thesis, and was therefore not used or followed in drafting the rendering above.
translator: original translation, drafted 2026-09-26 by WRITER-full-batch19, from Latin at farmer1998:27122
doctrine: The thesis argues that a Hebrew word for 'Man', spelled with He, Vau, and Aleph and applied to God, discloses by Cabala both the Trinity and the possibility of the Incarnation, agreeing, Pico says, with the Cabalists' own explicit statements and with the theology of Dionysius the Areopagite (farmer1998:27122). The immediately following thesis, 11>35, holds that God considered strictly in himself, as infinite and one, is on that consideration understood to proceed into nothing outside himself, but only to be enclosed within himself (farmer1998:27129).
not_established: A record in this packet nominally tied to Wirszubski's 'Conclusio xxxiv' states that it concerns 'the proper attitude at prayer', which does not match the content of this thesis (the divine name spelled He-Vau-Aleph); the packet flags this record as unresolved between 28.n and 11.n numbering, and it is not used as evidence here (wirszubski1989:3140).
